current_answer: As of 29 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. AI Stupid Level reports no below-baseline result among 25 API-tested models on its 24-hour boards as of 10:31 UTC; it says none of its 66 armed model-suite detectors fired, while nine are not yet armed. This is one monitor operator’s result, not a test of consumer chat surfaces or private workflows. BridgeBench’s latest visible NerfBench session remains 16 October: four series are inside its 90–110% band, and Opus 5.5 rose 10.1 percentage points from 9 to 16 October on a composite of correctness, output tokens, and cost. OpenAI’s October GPT-6 card reports selected safety regressions alongside factuality gains and less over-refusal; that is a narrow, provider-reported trade-off, not broad task decline. Anthropic’s Google Calendar connector errors on Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork were marked resolved at 18:52 UTC on 28 October. For a failed tool request, check the affected connector and status history; for a completed poor answer, repeat a safe task on the same surface, model selection, effort, and context, and score correctness separately from access, safety, cost, and correction time.

catalogue_card.question: Did a live monitor find a broad model drop today?
catalogue_card.text: Not on AI Stupid Level’s current API boards: it reports no below-baseline score among 25 models at 10:31 UTC. Nine of 75 model-suite detectors are not armed yet, and this does not test every chat app or user task.

summary: Broad capability decline across popular AI models is not established as of 29 October 2026.
AI Stupid Level reports no model below its recent baseline on 25 API-side 24-hour boards at 10:31 UTC; 66 of 75 model-suite detectors were armed and none fired, while nine were not yet armed.

BridgeBench’s NerfBench board still shows 16 October as its newest session; all four tracked scores remain inside its stated 90–110% band. Opus 5.5 rose 10.1 percentage points from 9 to 16 October, but the composite combines correctness, tokens, and cost.
OpenAI’s October GPT-6 system card reports selected safety regressions and improvements elsewhere, including factuality and reduced over-refusal; the tests are provider-authored and narrow.
Anthropic records Google Calendar connector errors from 26 October through 18:52 UTC on 28 October for Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork; this is a service-path event, not a completed-answer rating.
OpenAI’s 26 October GPT-6.1 Terra rollout may change model and effort presets for some eligible Work users; a rollout is not a matched quality test.

Recent English- and Spanish-language user posts describe context, instruction-following, task-completion, and usage-limit concerns, alongside positive or unchanged reports. They do not estimate prevalence.
For an individual failure, record the surface, selected model, effort, context, completion status, and any connector or quota error before changing providers.
uncertainty: AI Stupid Level is a monitor operator’s self-reported API-side benchmark. Its task set is private, its result was not independently reproduced here, and nine of its 75 model-suite detectors are younger than its ten-day arming requirement.
NerfBench’s latest visible session is 16 October, despite its stated three-tests-per-week schedule; the public board omits task-level outputs and correctness, token, and cost components.
Provider status records establish declared service events, not the route or recovery of an individual account.
Community reports are self-selected and mixed; they contain no representative denominator or matched task replay.
First-party pool analytics were unavailable, so reader use, return visits, switching, sharing, follows, and funding remain unknown.
